  B)      You are building a simple data entry module for a system that processes numerical  
  information. This module needs to take user input as a string and determine if it  
  represents a strictly positive integer. Additionally, for valid positive integers, the module (4)  
  should categorize them as either "small" (less than or equal to 100) or "large" (greater  
  than 100). Apply this condition with example program  
  
  C)      Give an example program to illustrate control statements in C++.                              (2)  
  2)           You are mentoring a junior developer who is implementing a stack-based feature for a  
  text editor's undo system. They have written the stack using a C-style struct with global  
  functions (like push, pop, and top).Rreview their code and suggest converting the  
  A)      implementation to a C++ class with member functions for better object-oriented design. (4)  
  Evaluate the benefits and potential drawbacks of using a C++ class with member  
  functions instead of a struct with global functions with stack implementation.  
  
  B)      Create a Rectangle class in C++ that encapsulates the following:                              (4)  
  Data:  
  
  • length (private, double)  
  • width (private, double)  
  
  
  Methods:  
  
  • setDimensions(double l, double w): Sets the length and width of the rectangle  
  (public). Include validation to ensure both length and width are positive values. If  
  invalid values are provided, display an error message and do not update the  
  dimensions.  
  • calculateArea(): Returns the area of the rectangle (public).  
  • calculatePerimeter(): Returns the perimeter of the rectangle (public).  
  • displayRectangleInfo(): Displays the length and width of the rectangle (public).

  B)          Analyse and write a program to implement virtual class concept by considering  
  following conditions  
  
  1. baseClass:  
  The baseClass has a virtual function display(). This means that in derived classes, a  
  function with the same name and parameters can override it.  
  
  2. derivedClass:  
  The derivedClass inherits from baseClass and overrides the display() function.  
  (4)  
  3. Polymorphism:  
  In main(), a derivedClass object is created, and its address is stored in a baseClass  
  pointer (ptr).  
  
  4. Output:  
  When ptr->display() is called, the derivedClass version of display() is executed,  
  demonstrating the dynamic binding (runtime polymorphism) achieved through virtual  
  functions.
